content_of_post_to_comment:
I'm 30, and while I'm working to achieve what I want out of life I can't help but to freak out about time passing, etc. My husband and I started working together on a project last year and his family who We live closest reacted almost hostile towards us after sharing it. That had such a negative impact in our life because we were already dealing with a lot of serious personal problems at the time and had no support network. The result? Our project got basically on pause because We, but specially my husband (because in his case it's his own parents and siblings gaslighting him), felt a deep sense of abandonment. And We just couldn't understand at the time why everybody we knew turned on us instead of feeling excited and being supportive. It's not like we got rich or anything. Since we are family We thought they would feel part of it, but I guess unfortunately that really hit a nerve in all of them. To the point where We have to pretend the project doesn't exist around them. It particularly affects me because my hidden talents are attached to this project while my husband already works on his own thing that it's already a stablished business. My husband said that he always had shared things he's working on with his family but he never had experienced that level of "withholding" combined with hostility and madness before. Which makes me think that I'm the reason they resent the project. The insecurity might be related to how they want to perceive us, people close to us don't like being surprised, just like that "Doug's Brainy Buddy" episode and/or there's something to do with envy of Couples who can work together on a business. But anyway, It doesn't matter the reason why.

The thing is now We got back on track committing to this project again. We learned the lesson of who we can trust the hard way. We are very confident, however We are still healing. And We still have intrusive thoughts from these experiences and others.. Because when we make progress there's very little people in our life we can share and celebrate with. In fact the people who are most supportive don't live close to us. My family is from another country, his friends are from another states. We tried to save money to move to a place where we can make new friends or be close to the people that are more supportive but we couldn't make that happen yet. That also was quite a distraction that piled up on our mental health. It's ridiculous how our brain can be so obnoxious when you are trying to grow. I have a scene in my mind that I'm on stage or on a race and all the toxic people I had in my life are watching me hoping for me to fail. As if I'm doing what I love not for myself but to show these people they were wrong? (That's silly, and I'm working on getting rid of that because that's a very negative motivation) I'm somehow allowing these ghost or demons with the face of the people who hurt or disappointed me to poke my brain with a pitchfork. I feel embarrassed that allowed them to affect me so much. I know I don't need anybody's approval but the social animal inside me feels very sad. I know that the world is not all schadenfreude, but it seems very real to me. What are your strategies to cope while working on your goals:

1- lack of support/ isolation/ discouragement/ withholding/ gaslighting

2- How to forgive myself for the time I wasted in a healthy way that is also realistic where I don't procrastinate my goals after saying it's okay that I didn't put the time before
